name: Guardian genius crossword No 269
preamble: Entrants must pick a side. The majority of down clues must have a letter removed before solving. These letters, taken in clue order, inform the solver of one who may not pick a side. Five further clues are ambiguous and four more are undefined.

clue.text: Fact US soldier embellished, at first, for VIP

indicators.note: at first asks only for the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: with its C removed the word reads Fat, and fat means big
GI is the standard term for an American soldier
its opening letter is the one used

explanation.surface: A report about an American soldier gets embroidered before it reaches a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The C taken out of 'Fact' starts the hidden message, leaving 'Fat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A biggie is slang for an important person or thing, a big shot.

clue.text: Support Dad winning Marlie's heart

indicators.note: to win something is to take it into your possession, so the word for Dad holds the letter

blocks.note: pop is an informal word for a father
without its L the name reads Marie, whose central letter is R

explanation.surface: A father backs his child after winning a girl's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the L from 'Marlie' to leave Marie; her middle letter is R.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is something that holds up a structure, a physical support.

clue.text: Powder starts to tickle Aunt Alisa's cheeks

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, all four of them

blocks.note: the opening letters of both words are used
with its A removed the name reads Lisa's, whose start is L
its opening letter is used, the last of the four starts

explanation.surface: Talcum powder on the cheeks tickles an aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Once the A of 'Alisa' is gone, 'Lisa' gives L, not A.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is the soft mineral ground into talcum powder.

clue.text: Elaborate system of gauze no good after minute

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter for good is dropped
after places the shortened word behind the abbreviation for minute

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for minute
with its U removed the word reads gaze, taken as written
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A detailed account of an intricate arrangement of surgical gauze.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the U from 'gauze' to read gaze; gaze without G is AZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A maze is an intricate network of paths, so it is a complex arrangement.

clue.text: Vestal college had setter regularly thrown out

indicators.note: every other letter is discarded at regular intervals, leaving the alternate ones

blocks.note: C is a standard abbreviation for college
with its D removed the word reads ha, taken as written
its first, third and fifth letters remain

explanation.surface: A college for vestal virgins expelled its compiler at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Vestal virgins were the priestesses of Vesta in ancient Rome, sworn to chastity.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestal as an adjective means pure or virginal, from the chaste priestesses of Vesta.

clue.text: Upturn in British trade — metal (old money) and sporting kit

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn reads the word from the bottom up, so it is reversed

blocks.note: to flog is British slang for to sell
B is the abbreviation for British
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
S stood for the shilling in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A boom in British trade in metal coins and sports equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the five ambiguous clues: the metal could equally be AL, aluminium, and the old money L, the pound, giving GOLF BALL on the Faithful side.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf bags hold the clubs a golfer carries, so they are part of the kit for that sport.

clue.text: Day endlessly difficult

indicators.note: endlessly strips the word of both its ends, leaving only its middle

blocks.note: FRI is the usual abbreviation for Friday
hard means difficult

explanation.surface: A day that is unremittingly hard.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the four undefined clues: a friar is one of the faithful, as 17 across says. Hard loses both its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar, a member of a religious order, is a fitting example of the faithful.

clue.text: Women into counterfeit Monets, perhaps

indicators.note: into puts the letter for women inside the word for forgeries

blocks.note: forged paintings by Monet would be fakes
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Women are drawn into a racket of counterfeit Impressionist paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the four undefined clues: Guy Fawkes, who plotted to blow up Parliament in 1605, is a traitor, as 17 across says.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Fawkes is the best-known English traitor, burned in effigy every Bonfire Night.

clue.text: Like a huntsman, cunning — stealing a new / old identity

indicators.note: stealing takes something in, so the word for cunning holds the letter

blocks.note: arch means slyly knowing or cunning
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
O is the abbreviation for old
ID is short for identity, as in an ID card

explanation.surface: A sly huntsman takes on a new identity in place of his old one.
explanation.walkthrough: The huntsman is a large spider, not a man with hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Arachnoid means spider-like, and the huntsman is a family of large spiders.

clue.text: Hoist e.g. Tesla or Ford's rear end up

definitions.note: with its I removed the word reads Host, a large crowd

indicators.note: the rear end of a word is its final letter
in a down clue going up reads the letters from the bottom, reversing them

blocks.note: a Tesla is an EV, an electric vehicle
taken as written
the name of the carmaker, of which only the last letter is used

explanation.surface: A car lift raises an electric car or the back of a Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from 'Hoist' to leave the definition, Host.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a large moving crowd, just as a host is a multitude.

clue.text: Salaries go back and forth, cast keep haggling

indicators.note: haggling is a tussle over terms, so these letters are fought over and rearranged

blocks.note: to wag is to move to and fro, like a dog's tail
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The cast of a show argue over pay, with talks swinging to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage packet is the envelope of pay, and by extension the earnings themselves.

clue.text: Tray of Chai (masala)

definitions.note: with its A removed the word reads Try, a verb

indicators.note: of says the answer is made from part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the answer runs across chai and masala, a spiced tea

explanation.surface: A tray bearing spiced Indian tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A from 'Tray' to leave the definition, Try.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim to do something is to try to do it.

clue.text: Haircut Henri rudely snipped

indicators.note: snipped cuts off the tail, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: frog is a rude name for a Frenchman, of whom Henri is an example

explanation.surface: A barber called Henri cut someone's hair carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fro is short for afro, a rounded mass of natural curls.
explanation.definitionFit: An afro, often shortened to fro, is a hairstyle.

clue.text: Outrageously we blame young female

indicators.note: something done outrageously is wild and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An indignant protest that a girl is being unfairly blamed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe lamb is a female lamb, a young female sheep.

clue.text: Parrot gawped, wings clipped

indicators.note: with its wings, the outer letters on either side, cut away only the middle remains

blocks.note: with its W removed the word reads gaped

explanation.surface: A clipped-winged parrot stared open-mouthed.
explanation.walkthrough: Parrot here is a verb: to repeat mindlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic them, just as to parrot is to copy words.

clue.text: Reveals, for audience, shoulders

indicators.note: for an audience the words are heard rather than read, so only the sound counts

blocks.note: to shoulder a burden is to bear it

explanation.surface: An outfit that shows off the shoulders, for the audience's benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the five ambiguous clues: either word can be the definition and the other the sound, so the Faithful side enters BEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare something is to uncover it, making it visible.

clue.text: Introduce official inside measurement, approximately 30 inches

indicators.note: inside puts the official within the measurement

blocks.note: a pace, a single step, is traditionally reckoned at about two and a half feet
ref is short for referee, a match official

explanation.surface: Bringing in an official to measure something about 30 inches long.
explanation.definitionFit: To preface a talk or book is to introduce it with opening remarks.

clue.text: Father Rafa insistent offence only taken on one side in Puerto Rico

indicators.note: only the letters at one edge of each word count, here the front edge, so the initials are used
in places these letters inside the abbreviation for the island

blocks.note: PR is the standard abbreviation for Puerto Rico
the initial of each of these three words is used

explanation.surface: A priest in Puerto Rico insists that Rafa's offence was entirely one-sided.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the five ambiguous clues: taking the other side, the last letters, gives ATE and so PATER, the Faithful side's answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior heads a priory and is addressed as Father, a title for a senior monk.

clue.text: 7 and 20 could be game show contestants

blocks.note: first meaning: betrayers, as Guy Fawkes and Judas at 7 and 20 down were
second meaning: the players on the reality show of that name

explanation.walkthrough: In The Traitors, hidden traitors try to eliminate the faithful; entrants pick a side, and the across answers at 7 and 20 suit the other choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Fawkes plotted against the king and Judas betrayed Jesus, so both are archetypal betrayers.

clue.text: Old volunteers I busted replaced — this may reveal bitterness

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve, renamed in 2014
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old soldier, busted and replaced, may well show some bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letter here is the whole word 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste buds on the tongue detect flavours, bitterness among them.

clue.text: Flapjack ingredient one of last two in BOGOF mate discovered

indicators.note: discovered means with its cover, the outer letters, taken off

blocks.clueFragment: one of last two in BOGOF
blocks.note: the last two letters of BOGOF are O and F, and the first is taken here
its inner letters are used

explanation.surface: A buy-one-get-one-free offer on flapjack ingredients, spotted by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the five ambiguous clues: BOGOF, buy one get one free, ends in O and F, and the F gives FAT, the Faithful side's answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flapjacks are baked bars of rolled oats bound with butter and syrup.

clue.text: Sent free advice once by retired writer

definitions.note: with the N removed this reads Set free

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word is reversed

blocks.note: rede is an archaic word for advice
the writer of the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Free advice sent long ago by an author who has since stopped writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the N from 'Sent' to read the definition, Set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem a captive is to buy their release, setting them free.

clue.text: Glyph in Calais attracting whistles from Londoners

blocks.note: Glyph is the setter, who would say I, and in French, as in Calais, that is je
in Cockney rhyming slang a whistle and flute is a suit

explanation.surface: The setter, in a French port, draws wolf-whistles from Londoners.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the four undefined clues: the Jesuits, the Society of Jesus, are among the faithful, as 17 across says.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jesuits, a Catholic order, are a fitting example of the faithful.

clue.text: Like Punch's wife — short, over the top

indicators.note: short means missing its last letter
in a down clue the shortened name sits over the top of the word for like

blocks.note: in the Punch and Judy puppet show, Punch's wife is Judy
as means like, as in 'as good as new'

explanation.surface: Punch's wife is brief and overdramatic.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the four undefined clues: Judas, who betrayed Jesus, is a traitor, as 17 across says.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver and is the byword for a traitor.

clue.text: Maybe fostered kin race around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: with its K removed the word reads in, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Relatives of a fostered child race around.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the K from 'kin' to leave 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fostered child is one example of a child in care, looked after by the state.

clue.text: Followers from Europe backtracking after concerning ITN broadcast

indicators.note: backtracking means going back, so the letters are reversed
after places the reversed letters at the end
broadcast scatters the letters, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
taken as written
EU is the European Union

explanation.surface: European fans go backwards after an ITN news broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: ITN is a British television news provider.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants who follow an important person.

clue.text: Bishop falls off zigzag slide on playing field

definitions.note: with the L removed this reads side on playing field, a noun phrase

indicators.note: falls off means drops away, so the letter is removed

blocks.note: a zigzag is a series of bends
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop tumbles off a winding slide in a playground.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the L from 'slide' to read the definition, side on playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: Each team defends one end of a pitch, so an end is a side of the field.

clue.text: Cuddle up in cheat's den with liberal European

blocks.note: with its E removed this reads chat's den, and a chat is a songbird whose home is a nest
L is the abbreviation for liberal
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Snuggling up in a swindler's hideout with a liberal from the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the E from 'cheat' to read chat, a small songbird such as the stonechat.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly against someone, to snuggle or cuddle up.

clue.text: Expected performance to end early

indicators.note: ending early cuts off the last letter

blocks.note: a duet is a performance by two players

explanation.surface: A show that was forecast to finish ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something due is anticipated or scheduled, so it is expected.

clue.text: Rewriting DNA history in smart way to reposition data sequences

indicators.note: rewriting sets the letters down afresh in a new order
in places these letters within the word for smart

blocks.note: cute can mean clever or sharp
taken as written
the past is history

explanation.surface: A geneticist rewriting DNA history neatly rearranges sequences of code.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut and paste is the computing operation that moves blocks of text or data.

clue.text: Mistakem? Yes and no!

blocks.note: the stray M is itself a slip of the keyboard, and once removed the clue asks for a word meaning mistake
the extra letter both is and is not an error: it is a slip in print and also the letter the puzzle hid on purpose

explanation.walkthrough: Remove the M from 'Mistakem' to read Mistake?; the clue as printed contains exactly what it asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing slip, a small mistake in printed or keyed text.

clue.text: Goat's hindquarters struck following a refusal — it's futile

indicators.note: struck off means removed, so the back end is deleted
following places the shortened animal after the refusal

blocks.note: no is a refusal
the animal, whose back end goes
the hindquarters of the word are its last two letters

explanation.surface: Hitting a goat on the rump after it refused to move is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letter is the whole word 'a' before 'refusal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go is something that cannot proceed, so attempting it is futile.

clue.text: Poor quality coordinates south of Paston's outskirts

indicators.note: in a down clue south of means below, so these letters come after
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: with its N removed the name reads Pasto's
x and y are the coordinates on a graph

explanation.surface: Shoddy mapping of a village on the edge of Paston.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the N from 'Paston' to read Pasto. Paston is a village in Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Poxy is British slang for worthless or shoddy.

clue.text: Tough to find a fitting place for this nerd, games ultimately challenging

definitions.text: Tough to find a fitting place for this

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

blocks.note: a square is someone conventional and unfashionable
PE, physical education, is school games
its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A geek is hard to place, since games are a challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is a square peg in a round hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A square peg is someone who does not fit in, from the idiom about a round hole.

clue.text: Organic material from waxy lemon

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the answer runs from the end of waxy into lemon

explanation.surface: Something organic extracted from a waxed lemon.
explanation.definitionFit: Xylem is the woody tissue that carries water through a plant.
